Write a config file

This lesson is fixture content, like the one before it. It carries a configuration block so that the parser checks have something to parse.

A block whose language maps to a config parser has to parse. A reader who copies a broken sample gets the same error you would, and a sample that never parsed was never run, so the surrounding prose is unlikely to describe what really happens.

Save the following as example-tool.yaml in the root of your project.

version: 1
plugins:
  - name: linter
    strict: true
  - name: formatter
    width: 88

The same idea applies to JSON. The checks pick the parser from the language, not from the file name, because a lesson often shows a fragment without naming a file at all.

{
  "version": 1,
  "plugins": ["linter", "formatter"]
}

Ask the tool to read the file back. Escape the angle brackets of any redirection you show, because a pre element is not a raw-text element and a browser parses an unescaped tag as real markup.

$ example-tool config show > config-dump.txt
$ example-tool config validate
config is valid
2 plugins loaded
